meta.title: When a Customer Comes In
meta.readFirst: Most failures in this chain are in the joins between stages, not the stages — though the money stages carry defects of their own. Eight places marked chain break below are where the system stops carrying your data forward and a human has to retype it — the spine on the left is interrupted at each one. Two more sit inside single steps rather than between them, in the Watch notes on steps 17 and 19.
meta.baseUrlHint: Every screen path on this page, like /report/business, opens against this address.
meta.mapLede: All twenty-seven steps in order. Hover or tab one to read the summary below the chart; click a step (or press Enter) to open its full operator guide — golden path, screens, fields, what the system writes, and screenshots. The five severed links are where the system stops carrying your data across.
meta.docLede: Every step in full, in order, with the chain breaks where they fall. The chart above is an index of what is written here — hovering a node shows you the step from this text, so the two can never disagree. Collapsed by default; it opens on its own when you follow a link to a step, and it always prints.
meta.colophon:
Method. Seven parallel readers over the shipped code — intake, quote, order, operations, documents, money, navigation — each report then adversarially verified against the cited files, and the surviving claims assembled into one ordered sequence.
Scope. Describes the system as built, not as intended. Steps are what a staff member does; the marked breaks are where the software stops helping.
Target chain. quote → order → fee entry → bill → invoice → write-off → month-end statement.
promptDecisions: Review and approval go through the audit engine (packages/api/src/modules/audit). The legacy `review` procedures on the routers are deliberate leftovers: do not build on them.
The web app is the only client that matters here. A server verb with no screen is a gap to close in the UI, not a reason to delete the verb.
Keep the existing shape: TanStack Router file routes, oRPC procedures, Drizzle schema, zod input schemas on both sides. No new libraries, no framework swaps.
Edit forms are patch semantics and an emptied box clears the stored value; create forms treat blank as "not given". Preserve that difference.

steps.title: Read the enquiry
steps.what: The enquiry arrives as an email thread in the three-pane mail client. Triage it — status, assign, note, archive — then reply, or compose a fresh first contact. SLA tiles show inbound volume and first-response rate against target.

watch.html: They came in any other way — only email lands in the inbox, so there is no thread to read. Go to step 2, or straight to step 5 for a repeat booking. An emailed enquiry that never converts leaves a thread but no outcome — a thread can only be closed, never marked won or lost — which is why win rate cannot be measured outside the quotation ledger.

steps.title: Create the customer
steps.what: Search the directory first. Then press Add: Company title is the only mandatory field, plus at least one role — Customer, Supplier or Agent. Saving takes you straight to the edit form’s seven sections, five of them new since the dialog: classification, address, settlement terms (days payable, credit limit), the internal staff slots and the record.

watch.html: Nothing forces this step — a quotation needs only a typed client name, so a walk-in can be quoted without ever existing as a company. Skipping it drops the buyer’s address, tax ID and payment terms from the invoice — those rows vanish, the name still prints. Duplicate protection is case-sensitive and there is no typeahead, so “Sunrise Sdn Bhd” and “SUNRISE SDN BHD” both save.

steps.title: Record the person who called
steps.what: Add the counterparty's human: name, role, phone, email, primary flag. This is the only real table for counterparty people — the seven “personnel” fields on the company record are NCT's staff, not theirs.

steps.title: Publish the rate card
steps.what: Build the pivoted tariff: billing-unit columns (20GP, 40HQ, 40RF), fee rows carrying destination, minimum charge and if-any flags, an amount in at least one column on every selling row — a single cell may be blank (unpriced) or N/A (not available at that unit). Bind it to a company to make it that customer's deal. Only an approved selling template counts as a tariff.

watch.html: The gate meant to stop an un-approved template being applied ships switched off, so nothing on the server refuses a draft card — only the picker’s default filter hides it, one tick away. Revising a card is Duplicate → edit → approve, then supersede the old one.

steps.title: Raise the quotation
steps.what: Fill the header: entrust unit, business type, incoterms, POL and POD, carrier, schedule, validity. Two remark fields — the annotation prints on the customer's sheet, the internal remark never does. Saving allocates NCT-Q-YYYYMM-#### and forces status to draft.

steps.title: Price it
steps.what: Record containers and batches. Then either tick tariff cells in the Reference-template dialog and apply them, or type fee lines by hand with side and segment. The FX table seeds each foreign line's rate; the footer computes the tax-inclusive total and estimated profit; each line gets a badge reading its price against the tariff.

watch.html: Applied lines always land at quantity 1. The template never reads your container mix, so on a 3×40HQ booking every applied line is a third of the real charge until you retype the quantity. Nothing checks the cost side at all, so the margin rests on unverified buy figures.

steps.title: Save against the tariff floor
steps.what: The server refuses the whole quotation if any selling line sits below its resolved tariff floor, and names every offending line. A price may be higher than tariff — never lower.

watch.html: Two approved sheets with the same start date that disagree on a price leave a line “ambiguous”, which carries no floor — the refusal silently skips it. Two spellings of one charge unit do the same.

steps.title: Get it approved
steps.what: Submit for review. The queue is the quotation ledger in review mode, routed by open audit stage rather than by status. A reviewer approves or rejects with a reason; approval freezes the record.

steps.title: Send it to the customer
steps.what: Pick your mailbox, the recipient (pre-filled from the company’s primary contact; Cc is always typed), format and language. The server re-renders the sheet, mails it as an attachment, opens a thread, links that thread to the quotation and stamps the send. The export is an allow-list: every cost line and the margin are stripped.

watch.html: There is no outbox. If the stamp fails after the mail goes out, the only way forward is pressing Send again — which mails the customer a second copy.

steps.title: Record their answer
steps.what: Read the reply in the Threads card, then mark Won or Lost with the date they actually answered, their PO reference and a note. The server refuses if the quotation was never sent, and freezes the record afterwards.

watch.html: A mis-keyed decision cannot be corrected. The code says so itself: fixing one currently needs a database edit. The customer never touches the system — there is no accept link and no signature capture.

steps.title: Convert the won quote into a job
steps.what: One press mints the order carrying the header, the company link, the containers and the receivable lines only — cost-side and if-any lines are deliberately left behind — then drops you on the order's edit form. It is one-shot: a quotation that already has an order is refused.

steps.title: Check the job number
steps.what: Conversion now stamps the next JOByymm##### serial by itself. Check the Job Number box. Only if it is blank — the org has no job-number sequence set up — press Assign number, under the Job Number box on the edit form or on the record page.

watch.html: A blank number after conversion means the org has no job-number sequence. Set one up in Parameters → Numbering rather than numbering jobs by hand, or every conversion will need this step.

steps.title: Receive it into operations
steps.what: The order lands unaccepted in the intake queue. Receive it, which stamps the acceptance time, or reject it with a reason. Re-receiving an accepted order is refused so the real receiving time survives.

steps.title: Fill in the operational detail
steps.what: One scrolling form with a section rail: business info, shipping space (vessel, voyage, ETD, ETA, ETB, cut-off), lading bills (shipper, consignee, notify, marks, weights), the desk roles, then containers, cargo lines, expense rows and appendages. Save sends only what changed and returns you to the trade ledger.

watch.html: No field on any trade is mandatory. A sea-import order saves with no client, no vessel, no ports and no cargo. The desk roles are free-typed names, not linked members — so the only way to ask “which orders are mine” is a substring search on a typed name — no member link, no my-orders view, and a namesake changes the answer.

steps.title: Get the order approved
steps.what: Submit from the trade ledger’s row menu; this queue only decides — one row, or a whole selection from its toolbar. One review queue spans every trade, not just sea export.

steps.title: Raise the bill of lading
steps.what: Type the B/L, or drop the carrier's PDF and let OCR pre-fill it. Point it at the job, then assign the bill's seven desk roles — unlike the order's, these are real linked members.

steps.title: Move the B/L through its states
steps.what: Check In (endorsement), Amend, Check Out (release) and Hold (detention), each with a cancel twin and each behind its own gate. Per row, or from the detail page — the list’s tick-boxes drive review only. Send the bill for review from Review on its page; while under review it is frozen. Scanned paperwork files as attachments on the bill itself.

steps.title: Approve the carrier's MBL/HBL
steps.what: Upload the PDF; the pipeline classifies, extracts and validates it, then either auto-approves or parks it for review. Check each field against the scan and approve. That approval is what starts automated customs and port tracking — nothing else does.

watch.html: There is no K1 or K2 customs-declaration type in the vocabulary, so the Sepangar filing itself lives outside this system.

steps.title: Watch the demurrage clock
steps.what: Two schedulers poll MYCIEDS and SBCP — customs three times a day, the port hourly — issuing three kinds of check. Customs clearance, vessel berthing and container gate-out arrive on their own, and the 72-hour countdown starts itself at berth. The board sorts by urgency and emails the owning branch on threshold and structural failures. A job the automation can never finish is voided with a written reason.

watch.html: Tracking jobs still store no order: a job finds its order, and an order its job, by B/L number. When two open jobs share one B/L number the order's card shows Match not certain and no clock, and where no portal login is saved the board says checks are off — nothing is being checked.

steps.title: Enter what the job cost and what it bills
steps.what: Two stacked grids, receivable above payable, saved together, with a live gross-profit box underneath showing both tax-inclusive and tax-exclusive. Copy to payable mirrors every named row across, minus the settlement party.

steps.title: Get the fees reviewed
steps.what: Submit from the fee ledger’s Review menu; someone else decides here, on a toolbar of Approved / Rejected / Refresh Page — nobody decides their own fee. The fee ledger’s own toolbar — not this one — carries reconcile, lock, archive, tag, and an exchange-rate dialog that applies a rate you type by hand.

steps.title: Group the fees into a bill
steps.what: Tick cost lines — or tick nothing, which means the whole filtered set — and press Create bill, optionally grouping by tax rate and splitting one bill per order. Mixed currency, attribute, settlement party or owning branch cannot land in one bill — the selection splits into one bill per combination.

steps.title: Get the bill approved
steps.what: This gate has teeth — for invoicing and write-off. Invoicing is frozen until the bill's latest review passes, and unlike the template gate at step 4 this one ships switched on. It also guards the bill itself: nothing on it saves while under review, and after approval only the paperwork (courier, voucher numbers, remark, tags) can change — removing a line is refused until the bill is dissolved and billed again.

steps.title: Issue the invoice
steps.what: Pick invoice category and type, optionally type the real tax-authority number, and accept or edit the amount — pre-filled with the outstanding balance, so partial invoicing works. The bill flips to invoiced once fully covered; a written-off bill with a balance left can be invoiced too and goes to Done.

watch.html: Over-limit invoicing needs a reason. When a covered bill's company is over its credit limit, the dialog names it and Issue Invoice stays disabled until a reason of at least 10 characters is typed; the reason goes to the audit log. A bill with no company, or a company with no limit, is never checked.

steps.title: Produce and hand over the document
steps.what: Preview the real document — seller (name, address, phone, contact — never a tax ID) and buyer (name, address, tax ID), fee lines with tax rate, two totals, payment terms from the bill's own term (the customer's current term only when no covered bill has one) — then save it as PDF or XLSX; the server records it as downloaded. A void reverses the whole allocation atomically and makes the bill re-invoiceable.

watch.html: The buyer block usually prints only a name — no address, tax ID or payment terms; see the break at step 20. There is also no send-by-email anywhere, although the quotation at step 9 has one, and no SST or GST: this is a commercial invoice, not a Malaysian tax invoice.

steps.title: Record the money and settle it
steps.what: Record the receipt — direction, settlement party, account, payment way, currency, amount, an exchange rate when the currency differs from the reporting one, bank slip, date — then verify it against a bill on its own side (a receipt settles receivables, a payment payables), or, from the same dialog, a single billed cost line. The amount spreads forward across that bill's cost lines in creation order. A payment can be edited while nothing live is settled against it; a wrong write-off is voided with a reason, not edited.

watch.html: Settlement attaches to the bill, never the invoice. With partial invoicing in use one bill legitimately carries several invoices — so “is this invoice paid?” has no answer on any screen, though both per-line splits exist to compute it.

steps.title: Close the month
steps.what: Tick cost lines and export the customer statement or debit note (one settlement unit each) or the per-shipment profit sheet. Then work the five Financial Stat tabs, whose months follow the branch's time zone: profit analysis, profit statement, receipts and payments, billing records, and ageing with days overdue plus a separate line for bills with no due date (credit limit appears only in the ageing export).

watch.html: The three month-end documents have no menu entry of their own — they open from an export dialog on two screens: the fee ledger (no ticks means the whole filtered set) and the order’s own expense page.

breaks.label: Inbox → Customer
breaks.body: An inbound email can be triaged, assigned and replied to, but never turned into a customer. The sender's name, address and domain get retyped by hand in step 2. The database already reserves customer as a link target; the router refuses it.

breaks.label: Documents → the job
breaks.body: Paperwork cannot be filed against the order it belongs to. The server accepts orders and ladings as link targets; the only screen that links anything sends the literal type quote. So the per-order Documents card queries a link nothing ever writes — and never renders at all, because the server sends documentCount and blStage while the client demands counts and customs.

breaks.label: The customer's identity ends here
breaks.body:
This is the most consequential break in the chain. The order knows its customer's company record. The fee line it creates does not — the settlement party is written as a bare string, and the company reference is not even an accepted field on this path.

The bill inherits that null, and the invoice at step 25 resolves its buyer from it. Result: the document your customer receives has no address, no tax ID and no due date. Someone retypes them outside the system, or it goes out incomplete.

breaks.label: Order → Bill
breaks.body: You cannot bill a job from the job. The order's expense page has no Create bill; its Cost Detail link opens the fee ledger already filtered to this order's unbilled fees, and the bill is created there.

breaks.label: The job never ends
breaks.body: A job can now be ended, and locked, one row at a time: End job, Cancel end, Lock job and Unlock job sit in the order row's menu and the reading pane, for members who hold the lifecycle rights. Shut out, archive and delete still have no screen, and there is no bulk action, so a year of old jobs is closed one by one.

chain.ariaLabel: Flow chart of the 27 steps in 5 phases, one phase per row. Three entry arrows point at steps 1, 2 and 5 depending on how the customer arrived. Step 4 is off-trunk setup feeding step 6. Step 10 branches: won continues to step 11, lost ends the chain. Four reject loops run backwards from steps 8, 15, 21 and 23. Step 27 is monthly, off the trunk. Five hand-offs are severed.

arrivals.title: How they arrive
arrivals.ariaLabel: Six arrival channels fanning into three entry points in the sequence: email starts at step 1, WhatsApp, walk-in, phone and agent nomination all join at step 2, and a repeat booking joins at step 5.
arrivals.hint: Hover or tab a channel — solid line = the system carries it, dashed = you transcribe it

channels.name: Email
channels.body:
The thread appears in the mail client on its own. Triage it, reply, and it stays attached to everything that follows — the quotation you send in step 9 opens a thread in the same place.

Requires an admin to have connected the mailbox first, or the Inbox is empty.

channels.name: WhatsApp
channels.body:
Most enquiry traffic in practice, and the system cannot see any of it. Read off what you need — company, contact, cargo, lane — and go straight to creating the customer.

Paste the substance of the chat into the company's remark field as you create it. That is the only place it will survive; there is no enquiry record to hold it.

channels.name: Walk-in
channels.body:
Someone at the Kolombong counter with a shipment. Take the details on paper or straight into the create-company dialog while they stand there — you will need company title, one role, a contact name and a phone number as a minimum.

Ask for the billing name and tax ID now, not later: by the time an invoice needs them the fields are three screens away from whoever is typing.

channels.name: Phone
channels.body: Same as a walk-in, with nothing to show them. Take the enquiry, create the customer, then email them the quotation so the chain acquires a written trail it otherwise never gets.

channels.name: Agent nomination
channels.body:
An overseas agent or co-loader nominates the shipment to NCT. The customer here is the agent, not the shipper — create them with role Agent and record the shipper separately, or the invoice goes to the wrong party.

Their rate is usually a standing arrangement, so check for an existing deal card bound to them before quoting fresh.

channels.name: Repeat booking
channels.home: No enquiry record — but the customer is already on file
channels.body:
An existing customer with another shipment — most of the volume. They are already in the directory and their deal card is already bound, so skip creation entirely — press Duplicate on their last quotation, or raise a fresh one. Duplicate on an order row instead makes a new numbered order with no fees and skips straight to receiving it into operations at step 13.

Check the deal card's validity dates first. An expired card silently falls back to the standard tariff, and the price you quote changes without warning.

arrivals.converge: From the quotation onward there is one path, and it is the numbered sequence below. Whatever channel they came in on, the work after step 5 is identical — which is also why, outside email, the enquiry itself leaves no record, and even an email thread never records whether it was won or lost.

golden.action: Type an internal note in **Add an internal note…**
golden.detail: Notes are staff-only and never go to the customer.

golden.action: For a first contact, press **New email** at the top of the left rail instead

golden.detail: **Unarchive** reverses it. **Mark unread** puts it back in someone's queue.

routes.label: Full company edit form — where Create lands you

guide.navigate: Top nav **Sales** → **Companies**
before: Have the company's legal name exactly as it should print on documents.
Search first. The duplicate check only catches an exact same-case name.

golden.action: Open **Sales → Companies**
golden.detail: The directory lists every company, with role segments **Customers**, **Suppliers** and **Overseas agents**.

golden.action: Type the name into **Search name, EN name, code, customer code** and check for an existing record
golden.detail: The search matches substrings in all four fields. There is no typeahead warning when you add a company.

golden.action: Not found? Click **Add** in the toolbar
golden.detail: The **Add company** dialog opens.

golden.action: Type the **Company title**
golden.detail: This is the only required field. Leaving it blank shows **Required**.

golden.action: Optionally fill **Code** and **Customer code**
Under **Roles**, keep **Customer** ticked (it is ticked by default); add **Supplier** or **Overseas agent** if they apply
golden.detail: The server refuses a company with no role: **A company needs at least one role (customer, supplier or agent)**.

golden.action: Press **Create and continue**
golden.detail: A toast reads **Company created — add the rest of its details** and you land on the full edit form. A same-name company is refused with **A company with this name already exists in the directory**.

golden.action: Use the section rail to fill **Identity** → **Roles & status** → **Classification** → **Address** → **Settlement** → **People** → **Record**
golden.detail: The fields that reach the invoice are in **Address** and **Settlement** (**Days payable**, **Credit limit**, **Settlement currency**). **People** holds NCT's own staff for this account, not the customer's.

golden.action: Press **Save changes** (header or form foot)
golden.detail: The header counter shows **N unsaved** until you save. A toast reads **Company updated** and you land on the company record page. On this form, an emptied box clears the stored value.

fields.note: At least one. Customer is pre-ticked

Every section's fields on Save changes

fixes.title: Duplicate companies enter through case
fixes.why: The unique index is on the raw name, so "Sunrise Sdn Bhd" and "SUNRISE SDN BHD" both save. Two records then split one customer's quotations, orders and ageing, and neither shows the true exposure.
fixes.repair: Make the unique index case-insensitive (lower(name)) and offer a typeahead of near matches in the Add dialog before the save is attempted.

pitfalls: The seven personnel fields on the company edit form are NCT's own staff, not the customer's people. Record the customer's people here.

fixes.title: A contact nobody ticked as Primary never reaches the collections call list
fixes.why: The Add contact dialog defaults Primary to false and nothing promotes the first contact on a company, but the month-end ageing DETAIL sheet joins companyContact strictly on isPrimary = true with no fallback. A company with three recorded contacts and no ticked primary prints empty Contact / Role / Phone / Email columns on the 催收 sheet, so the collections clerk re-looks the number up in the company record — the one job the contacts table was added for.
fixes.repair: Either auto-promote in companyContacts.create (before the insert, if the company has no existing is_primary row, force isPrimary = true), or make report.ts fall back to the oldest contact when none is primary (DISTINCT ON / lateral ordered by is_primary desc, created_at asc instead of the flat eq(isPrimary, true) predicate).

routes.label: Template editor ("new" for a fresh one)
Expense template review queue (Approvals → Expense template)

guide.navigate: Top nav **Sales** → **Fee templates**; approve under **Approvals** → **Expense template**
before: This is one-off setup, not part of every shipment. Do it when a new standard tariff or a customer-specific deal is agreed.
Have the charge names ready. The **Cost Name** box suggests entries from **Sales → Cost items**.

golden.action: Open **Sales → Fee templates** and press **Add**
golden.detail: The editor opens as **New Fee Template**.

golden.action: In **Basic Information**, fill **Template Name *** and **Business Type ***
golden.detail: These two are required. **Template name is required** appears if the name is blank.

golden.action: Set **Fee Type** to **Selling Price**
golden.detail: Only an approved Selling Price template acts as a tariff floor. **Cost** templates price the buy side.

golden.action: For a customer's own deal, pick them in **Client** ("Start typing to search the directory")
golden.detail: Leave Client empty for the company-wide standard tariff. Optionally set **Shipping Type**, **Carrier**, **Booking Agent**, **Foreign Agent**, **Settlement Unit**, **Valid From**, **Valid To** and **Annotation**.

golden.action: In **Fee Details**, press **Add Billing Unit** once per container size
golden.detail: Type each column header, e.g. `20GP`, `40HQ`, `40RF`. A billing unit cannot be blank or repeated.

golden.action: Press **Add Fee** for each charge and fill the row

fixes.title: A quotation stays fully editable while it is sitting in the reviewer's queue
fixes.why: quotations.update guards only two things - decidedAt (a won/lost quote) and assertPostApprovalEditable (an already-passed review). It never calls assertNotUnderReview, the guard gates.ts:130 was written for exactly this and which lading.ts:1474 and company.ts:1343 do call. So after Submit for review the salesperson can reopen /quotations/$quotationId, rewrite every selling line and save; the submission stays under_review with the old submit stamp, and the branch manager's Approved in /approve/quotation signs a price sheet that no longer exists. modules/audit/gates.ts:123 asserts a quotation is already safe 'by its own private route, assertDraft inside loadScopedDraftLine' - that function is routers/quote.ts:78, in the legacy quote router, and never runs on the quotation path, so the claimed protection is not there. quotations.applyTemplate (:3519) has the same hole.

fixes.title: The seeded quotation flow lets the branch manager approve their own quotation
fixes.why: The seeded Quotation review flow's only stage targets role branch-manager with quorum any_pass_all_reject - one approval carries it. roles.ts:102 grants branch-manager the whole `quotation` subtree, i.e. both quotation.update (the submitNode, resources.ts:124) and quotation.review (the reviewNode). Nothing in decide() compares org.membership.id with submission.submittedBy; the only ownership test in the engine is withdraw.ts:48. A branch manager therefore prices a quote, presses Submit for review, opens /approve/quotation and presses Approved on their own row; the convert_order gate then opens and the quote becomes an order with no second pair of eyes. The same seed file rejects this arrangement explicitly for customer (seed.ts:83-89, 'approving their own edit, which is the exact property director exists to provide') and for lading (:160), so quotation is the one trigger that shipped with the pattern the others were fixed to avoid.
fixes.repair: Refuse self-decision in decide(): after loading the submission, throw FORBIDDEN when submission.submittedBy === org.membership.id, the same shape as withdraw.ts:48. Or point the seeded quotation stage at `director`, as the customer/supplier/agent/lading flows do.

fixes.title: The legacy quotations.review verb stamps 'approved' with no submission behind it
fixes.why: quotations.review still writes quotation.auditStatus straight through canAuditTransition, filing no audit_submission row. No page in apps/web calls it any more, but it is a live oRPC procedure held by branch-manager and director. Because the gates read audit_submission (gates.ts:90) while the ledger badge and the /approve/quotation audit-status filter read the cache column, the two can be made to disagree permanently: a quotation reads 'Approved' with 'Approve staff' blank in every list, while convertToOrder refuses with '"Convert order" requires review approval first' and nothing in the UI explains why or offers a way out.
fixes.repair: Delete quotations.review now that engineReview routes every UI path through auditReview.*; if a legacy caller must survive, re-implement it as a thin wrapper over submitForReview/decide so audit_submission stays the only writer of the review cache.

fixes.title: Submit-then-retract permanently unlocks an approved, frozen record with no reviewer involved
fixes.why: Every seeded flow sets postApprovalEditable: false (seed.ts:232), so assertPostApprovalEditable freezes an approved quotation against editing. But it only fires when the LATEST submission is `passed` (post-approval.ts:43), and submitForReview happily opens a new attempt on an approved record. retract() then succeeds because that new attempt is under_review (withdraw.ts:51), leaving the latest status `withdrawn` - at which point the freeze is inert forever and, per the first finding, the record was editable throughout. Whoever holds quotation.update can therefore rewrite an approved quotation's prices alone, in three clicks. The same sequence unlocks an approved collective order.
fixes.repair: Either refuse submitForReview when the latest submission is `passed` and the flow's postApprovalEditable is false (force an explicit unlock), or key assertPostApprovalEditable on 'this resource has a passed submission not superseded by a later passed one' rather than on the latest attempt's status alone.

fixes.title: A collective order stays fully editable while it is awaiting the reviewer's decision
fixes.why: collectiveOrder.update guards `locked` and assertPostApprovalEditable and never calls assertNotUnderReview - the string does not appear anywhere in routers/collective-order.ts. Step 14's operational detail (vessel, ports, cargo, container counts, client) can therefore be rewritten after the trade-ledger row menu's Submit for review and before accounting presses Approved in /approve/order, and the submission carries no content hash or version to notice. The reviewer approves a shipment they never saw, and the approval stamps land on the edited row as if they covered it. saveChildren (:4756) and assignJobNumber (:2800) have the same gap.
fixes.repair: Call assertNotUnderReview(tx, organizationId, "collective_order", orderId) in collectiveOrder.update, saveChildren and assignJobNumber, right beside each existing assertPostApprovalEditable call.

fixes.title: Order approval freezes nothing downstream, so approving or rejecting an order changes nothing operational
fixes.why: The seeded 'Order review' flow ships enabled with `gates: []`. Nine gate keys are declared for collective_order (modules/collective-order/gates.ts:36) and not one is ticked, so assertGatesCleared returns early at gates.ts:85 for every verb. Raising the bill of lading - step 16 - is not even in the vocabulary: lading.create (routers/lading.ts:1030) resolves the order via resolveLadingOrder and never reads orderAuditStatus or any submission. So an order that is unsubmitted, under review, or explicitly REJECTED can still be locked, ended, exported, have costs booked against it, and have a B/L raised and released on it. Accounting's rejection in /approve/order is a badge on a row and nothing more: no verb anywhere consults it, so a rejected shipment proceeds to the carrier and onto the customer's invoice unimpeded.
fixes.repair: Tick the gate keys the flow is meant to enforce in SEEDED_FLOWS' collective_order entry (at minimum expense_entry and end_order), and declare plus wire a `create_lading` gate: defineGates it in modules/collective-order/gates.ts and call assertGateCleared(db, organizationId, "collective_order", orderId, "create_lading") in lading.create once resolveLadingOrder has produced an order id.

history.note: Fixed: the Order flow now seeds the lock, end_order, shut_out and create_lading gates, and lading.create enforces create_lading. Still broken: those gates are seeded only for new orgs (gatesOnlyForNewOrg), so existing orgs keep an ungated flow. expense_entry is deliberately left unticked, so costs can still be booked against a rejected order.

fixes.title: The legacy collectiveOrder.review verb lets ops stamp their own order approved outside the queue
fixes.why: collectiveOrder.review writes collective_order.order_audit_status directly through canAuditTransition and files no audit_submission. roles.ts grants ops the whole `collectiveOrder` subtree - collectiveOrder.update AND collectiveOrder.review - so an ops member can move their own order draft to pending to approved on this endpoint without ever appearing in /approve/order, whose listing is driven by awaitingMyReview over submissions. The order ledger's Audit status column and its audit-status filter read the column this writes, so the row displays as reviewed, the submissions table holds nothing, and nobody in accounting ever saw it. order-row-actions.tsx:55 records that the last UI caller was removed on 2026-09-09; the procedure itself was left in place.
fixes.repair: Delete collectiveOrder.review (apps/web/src/architecture.test.ts already forbids a UI caller), or reduce it to a wrapper over submitForReview/decide so audit_submission remains the only writer of order_audit_status.

fixes.title: A bill of lading can be set to Released or On-hold from a dropdown, skipping the release / detention gates
fixes.why: The workflow verbs are gated: check-out calls assertGateCleared(..., "release") and hold calls it with "detention" (packages/api/src/routers/lading.ts:633), which is how a tenant makes cargo release require an approval. But `status` is an ordinary writable column on create and update, and both forms offer the gated states directly: STATUS_OPTIONS = [draft, confirmed, released, cancelled, on-hold] (apps/web/src/routes/_next/lading/create.tsx:140, apps/web/src/routes/_next/lading/$id/edit.tsx:165). Picking Released on the edit form writes status='released' straight through (lading.ts:1556-1602) with no gate and no release decision recorded, and checkedOutAt stays NULL, so the list and the record read as released while the detail page still offers Check Out and the configured release approval never ran. Picking On-hold is worse: heldAt stays NULL, so Cancel Hold refuses with 'Not on hold' (lading.ts:585) and the bill is stuck displaying a hold nobody can lift except by another free status edit.
fixes.repair: Make status non-free-set for the workflow-owned states: narrow the create/update zod field to z.enum(["draft","confirmed","cancelled"]) and refuse released/on-hold/amended with a message naming the workflow verb, and drop those three from STATUS_OPTIONS in both forms, so the only way into them is checkOut / hold / amend, which carry the gates and the stamps.

history.note: Both forms now offer only draft, confirmed and cancelled. On the server, create and update call assertSettableStatus on any status change.

fixes.title: A bill of lading under review stays fully editable, so the reviewer approves content that changed after they read it
fixes.why: lading.update runs only assertPostApprovalEditable (packages/api/src/routers/lading.ts:1554), which fires after a submission has PASSED. The window while a submission is open is what assertNotUnderReview covers, and this very file imports it (lading.ts:34) and calls it in delete (lading.ts:1474) and bulkDelete (lading.ts:1513). It is absent from update. So a B/L can be submitted for review and then have its bill number, shipper, consignee, containers, weights and status rewritten while it sits in the reviewer's queue; the reviewer approves whatever is there when they click, and the post-approval freeze then locks in the rewritten version. This is the failure the gates module documents as TC-138 (packages/api/src/modules/audit/gates.ts:103-128): 'If it can change in between, they have approved something they never saw.' You cannot delete a B/L under review, but you can rewrite every field of it.
fixes.repair: Add `await assertNotUnderReview(context.db, organizationId, "lading", ladingId);` beside the assertPostApprovalEditable call in lading.update, matching delete/bulkDelete.

history.note: lading.update now calls assertNotUnderReview before assertPostApprovalEditable.

fixes.title: OCR validation issues are computed, returned, and thrown away by the create form
fixes.why: uploadOcr returns the extraction engine's ValidationIssue[] alongside the fields (packages/api/src/routers/lading.ts:1965, built in ocrExtractionForForm at lading.ts:2418) - codes container_check_digit, crossfoot_mismatch, missing_required, each with severity 'error' or 'warning' (packages/document-ai/src/registry/types.ts:30-43); the issue COUNT is even written to the audit trail. The client drops them: the ocrResult state type declares only { confidence, rawText, fields, containers } (apps/web/src/routes/_next/lading/create.tsx:293-298) and nothing in the OCR tab renders an issue. Apply to Form (create.tsx:312-349) then writes every extracted value - grossWeight, chargeableWeight, volumeCbm, containerQty and the whole container table - unconditionally, and the button is enabled at any confidence, including 10%. A container number that fails its check digit, or a weight that fails the crossfoot check, lands on a document of title with no signal; the operator sees one aggregate 'Confidence: N%' and a list of values that look verified.
fixes.repair: Add `issues: ValidationIssue[]` to the ocrResult state type, render them against their fields in the extracted-fields grid (error / warning styling), and disable Apply to Form - or require an explicit 'apply anyway' acknowledgement - while any issue has severity 'error'.

history.note: OCR issues are now kept in state and shown next to their fields. Apply to Form is disabled while any issue has severity error, unless the clerk ticks an acknowledgement.

fixes.title: Linking the approved order carries only its job number; every shipment detail the order already holds is retyped onto the B/L
fixes.why: Picking the linked order sets orderId and copies picked.jobNumber into orderNo, and nothing else (apps/web/src/routes/_next/lading/create.tsx:1243-1252). The order just linked already holds a matching value for most of the bill: vesselName, voyage, portOfShipment, portOfDestination, transitPort, etd, eta, atd, mbl, hbl, soNo, clientName, entrustUnit, tradeTerms, shipCompany (packages/db/src/schema/collective-order.ts:125-220), and lading has a column for each (vessel, voyage, pol, pod, transhipmentPort, etd, eta, atd, mblNo, hblNo, bookingNo, entrustUnit, tradeTerm, shippingCompany - packages/db/src/schema/lading.ts:44-110). All of it is typed again by hand across a five-tab form, on the screen that already knows the order id. Beyond the keystrokes the two records drift: the B/L and the order it documents can name different vessels, ports or ETDs with nothing reconciling them, and the B/L is the one that prints.
fixes.repair: On order select, fetch collectiveOrder.get for the picked id and prefill the still-empty B/L fields from it (vessel/voyage/pol/pod/etd/eta/mblNo/hblNo/bookingNo/entrustUnit/tradeTerm/shippingCompany), leaving anything already typed alone, and mark which values came from the order so they can be overridden knowingly.

fixes.title: The 'fees must pass review before billing' gate is silently skipped whenever the operator bills without ticking rows
fixes.why: createBill resolves the selection first - ticks, or the whole filter result set when nothing is ticked - into `costLineIds` (packages/api/src/routers/expense/cost-lines.ts:2448). Every guard afterwards uses the resolved rows, except the review gate, which is handed the RAW input array: assertGatesCleared(context.db, organizationId, "cost_line", input.costLineIds, "create_bill") (cost-lines.ts:2502-2508). On the unticked path input.costLineIds is [] and assertGatesCleared returns immediately on an empty array (packages/api/src/modules/audit/gates.ts:76). So a tenant that turned on the opt-in rule that every fee must have PASSED review before billing has it enforced when rows are ticked and bypassed when they are not - which is the path the UI actively promotes for large selections ('Create Bill (全选)', apps/web/src/routes/_next/expenses/cost-lines.tsx:2214). Never-submitted fees get billed and invoiced, with no error, because the gate returned clean.
fixes.repair: Pass the resolved selection: assertGatesCleared(context.db, organizationId, "cost_line", costLineIds, "create_bill").

history.note: createBill now passes the resolved costLineIds to the create_bill gate instead of input.costLineIds.

fixes.title: An approved fee's exchange rate can still be rewritten in bulk, past the post-approval freeze
fixes.why: costLines.update runs postApprovalGate (packages/api/src/routers/expense/cost-lines.ts:137-142, 333-339), so once a review has passed and the flow says post_approval_editable = false (the schema default, packages/db/src/schema/audit.ts:145) an approved fee refuses every edit with 'This record was approved and its content can no longer be edited'. exchangeRateBatch - the fee grid's bulk FX edit - does not use the governed writer and runs no such gate (cost-lines.ts:2063-2166). Its only filter is isClaimed, which looks at billId, invoicedAmount, writtenOffAmount, lockedAt and recPayLockedAt and nothing about review (packages/api/src/routers/expense/batch.ts:116-124). So an approved, unbilled fee has its FX rate - and with it the local-currency value that the bill and every base-currency total read - changed in bulk by any holder of costLine.update, with no re-review and the approved stamp untouched. The single-row path refuses the same edit.
fixes.repair: Run the post-approval gate over the selection in exchangeRateBatch (assertPostApprovalEditable per row, or route the write through costLineWriter's `update` verb), and put approved-frozen rows into the existing `skipped` report so the operator sees which lines were left behind and why.

history.note: exchangeRateBatch now loads the review freezes and skips rows that are under review or approved-frozen, reporting them with a reason.

fixes.title: An approved fee can be deleted outright - approval binds its content but not its existence
fixes.why: The delete verb's gates are deleteRefusalsGate, orderUnlockedGate and splitsReleaseGate (packages/api/src/routers/expense/cost-lines.ts:427-431); the batch delete path repeats the same three refusals by hand (cost-lines.ts:1774-1795). Neither consults the review state - the refusals are billed / locked / rec-pay-locked only. So a fee that has been submitted, reviewed and APPROVED, and is therefore cleared for billing, can be deleted before it reaches a bill by any holder of costLine.delete, with no re-review and no signal to the approver. The asymmetry is the tell: the same fee cannot have its amount edited to 0 (postApprovalGate refuses) but can be removed entirely. On the receivable side that is approved revenue that simply never gets billed.
fixes.repair: Add postApprovalGate to the writer's `delete` verb and an equivalent assertPostApprovalEditable sweep to the batch delete branch, so an approved fee must be taken back out of approval before it can be removed - the contract update already enforces.

evidence.quote: const freezes = await costLineReviewFreezes(tx, organizationId, ids);

history.note: The writer's delete verb, the batch delete branch and saveChildren's removal path all refuse approved and under-review fees now. Deleting the parent order does not. collectiveOrder.delete and the order batch delete call clearOrderCostLines, which checks only billed/settled/locked and then hard-deletes every fee on the order, approved ones included, without consulting fee review state.

fixes.title: A fee sitting in the review queue is fully editable, so the approval lands on an amount the reviewer never saw
fixes.why: The costLineWriter update gates are postApprovalGate, singleFeeLockGate, recPayLockGate, billedFieldsGate and orderUnlockedGate (packages/api/src/routers/expense/cost-lines.ts:333-339). postApprovalGate only fires once a submission has PASSED. The open window - submitted, awaiting a decision - is what assertNotUnderReview exists for, and the gates module states why it is not optional: 'a reviewer opens a record, reads it, and approves it. If it can change in between, they have approved something they never saw' (packages/api/src/modules/audit/gates.ts:103-128). Across the API it is called only from company.ts (contract), lading.ts (delete/bulkDelete) and quotation.ts (fee_template); cost_line is covered nowhere. So a fee can be submitted at RM 500, edited to RM 5,000 while it sits in /approve/cost, approved on the reviewer's next click, and then frozen at the new number by the post-approval rule. The trail shows an approval and a separate edit, with nothing saying the approval was of the pre-edit figure.
fixes.repair: Add an assertNotUnderReview gate to the costLineWriter `update` verb (and to exchangeRateBatch and delete once those are gated per the findings above), so a fee under review refuses edits with the existing 'retract the submission first' message.

ledger.title: What to fix first
ledger.lede: The seven nouns of the chain — quote, order, fee, bill, invoice, write-off, statement — each have a real table, a real router and a real screen. Most of what is missing is the arrows between them; the money stages also get their own arithmetic wrong. Ranked by consequence:

items.title: The customer’s identity does not survive the journey
items.body: Carried onto the order, dropped at the cost line. The invoice still prints the buyer’s name but loses the address, tax ID and payment terms — and with no settlement company, the bill never gets a due date.

items.title: Every cross-currency settlement books a fabricated exchange gain or loss
items.body: The payment form has no exchange-rate field, so every payment is stored at a rate of 1 and cannot be corrected. The write-off derives its settled rate from that, so a payment settled against a bill in a different currency posts a gain or loss that never happened — unless the payment is already in the branch’s reporting currency.

history.note: The payment form now sends an exchange rate. The write-off treats a stored payment rate of 1 as unknown and looks the rate up in the org table instead. settlementFx books no gain or loss when a rate is unknown, and reports which rate was missing (fxUnknown).

items.title: Bills from the happy path can never become overdue
items.body: No settlement company reaches the bill, so the payment-terms trigger never fires and the due date stays empty. Ageing counts days overdue from the due date alone, so these bills show a blank Days overdue, sort last, and never trip the workbench’s Overdue chip — finance reads “nothing is late” on money that is.

items.title: Conversion turns every fee into a lump sum
items.body: Quantity and unit price exist on the quotation fee line and on the cost line, and the invoice and month-end statement both print them. The bridge carries neither, so those columns print blank on every job that started as a quote.

history.note: The quote-to-cost-line bridge now carries quantity and unit price whenever quantity x price equals the amount. Only lines raised to a minimum charge stay as lump sums, and that is deliberate.

items.title: One shipment, two profits
items.body: The order’s gross-profit box and the per-shipment profit sheet use the fee row’s rate; Financial Stat uses the bill’s rate, dated the moment the bill was grouped. The same job reports two different margins depending on which screen you ask.

items.title: An approved bill’s total can still be rewritten
items.body: The bill flow ticks two of its six gates, and the two it skips protect the signed figure: a bill under review can have its fee set shrunk, and the re-total after removing a line carries no post-approval freeze, so an approved total can be rewritten downward. Booking a write-off needs a signature; reversing one needs none.

history.note: Fixed: the retotal writer is now blocked while the bill is under review and frozen after approval, and header edits are blocked during review. Still broken: the seeded bill flow still ticks only two gates. cancel_write_off is wired into write-offs.reverse but not seeded, so under the default flow a write-off can still be reversed with no approval.

items.title: There is no organisation base currency
items.body: Currency is set per branch. Every total summed across branches adds MYR to VND and returns a number with no unit; the same-currency guard only protects a single bill.

history.note: Fixed: there is now an optional org base currency (org_setting.base_currency), and the Financial summary warns when branch currencies are mixed. Still broken: the setting is nullable, and when unset reportingCurrency falls back to the branch currency. Cross-branch roll-ups still add bills converted into different currencies; the new warning flags this but the figures are unchanged.

items.title: Conversion still produces an unnumbered job
items.body: Assign number now sits on the edit form conversion lands you on, so it is harder to miss — but conversion allocates nothing, and the lines it created keep the quotation number. One shipment’s invoice can print two different order numbers.

history.note: convertToOrder now allocates a job number through insertOrderWithJobNumber. The carried cost lines take that job number and fall back to the quotation number only when no job sequence exists.

items.title: A shipment can never be closed

items.body: WhatsApp and agent nominations have nowhere to land; walk-ins and phone calls can be typed straight into a company or a quotation, but leave no enquiry behind. Even an emailed enquiry has no outcome — a thread can only be closed, never marked won or lost.

items.title: Money leaves by hand at both ends
items.body: No invoice email and no invoice permalink, and settlement applies to bills rather than invoices — so “is this invoice paid?” has no answer on any screen, though the per-line splits exist to compute it.

items.title: Nothing enforces the shape of a job

items.title: Credit is captured and never enforced
items.body: Credit limit is stored, shown on the company record, and printed only in the ageing report’s exported spreadsheet. No code computes exposure, and invoicing never consults it.

items.title: The invoice is not a Malaysian tax invoice

items.title: Haulage is a separate island

items.title: The accountant who submits a bill can sign its first review stage themselves
items.body: Step 21 stops the person who submitted a fee from approving it. Step 23 does not do the same for the bill built from those fees. The bill resource has separationOfDuties set to false, so decide.ts never checks whether the reviewer is the submitter, and the queue filter does not hide the reviewer's own submissions. The seeded Bill review flow puts the accounting role on stage 1 ('all must pass'). The accounting role holds the whole expense subtree, so the same accountant has expense.bill.update to submit and expense.bill.review to decide. In an org with one accountant, that person groups the fees, submits the bill and passes stage 1 alone, which defeats the 'two sets of eyes on the figures' the flow promises. The bill then goes to invoicing and write-off with only the director's stage 2 behind it. The project's own concurrency test says it outright: an owner may review a bill they submitted.

items.title: Before 8 am the payment date and decision date default to yesterday
items.body: The Add Payment dialog (step 26) pre-fills Pay and Receive Date, and the Decide dialog (step 10) pre-fills Decision date, with new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10). That is the UTC calendar date. In Malaysia (UTC+8), anything recorded between 00:00 and 07:59 local time silently gets the previous day. A receipt keyed by the cashier early on the 1st of the month is dated the last day of the prior month, so it lands in the wrong month in Financial Stat and the month-end pack. A Won/Lost entered early in the morning gets the wrong decision date. The field looks correctly filled, so it is rarely checked.
